current_status.from: Active as of 2026-09-23; set to expire 2026-11-17 absent extension. City Manager David Cameron has indicated city staff will seek a council vote to extend the moratorium. On 2026-09-17, NSI A.1 LLC (developer Trent Overhue, also a party to moratorium disputes in Benton County and involved in a Webster County data center) sued the City of Springfield in Greene County Circuit Court, arguing the moratorium (Ordinance 28306) was improperly enacted as an 'administrative delay'/interim zoning measure without the notice-and-hearing process Missouri law requires for zoning changes, and separately alleging a City Charter defect in how the measure was filed. NSI is asking the court to invalidate the moratorium, or at least lift it as applied to its pre-development application for a data-processing use at 2900 S. National Ave. No ruling had been reported as of 2026-09-23.

outcome.from: TA-2026-01 was ultimately approved: the City Council passed the permanent data-center ban 7-1 on 2026-05-20 (two members absent), defining data centers, excluding them from the warehouse-use category, and prohibiting permitting/conditional-use approval for them in all zoning districts. The specific 2026-04-13 Planning and Zoning Commission vote tally that preceded Council action was not independently located -- no separate minutes document for that meeting has been posted, and no news account reporting that specific vote was found -- but the case clearly advanced favorably from P&Z to Council given the subsequent 2026-05-20 passage.
outcome.to: City Council passed the permanent data-center prohibition May 19, 2026, followed by mayoral approval May 20. The ordinance recites the planning commission April 13 recommendation, 7-3. The permanent instrument and its exact legal relationship to Resolution 25-014 require separate treatment.
outcome.reason: Separate legislative passage, mayoral approval, recommendation and the unverified prior-pause termination relationship.
